originalTitle: Suri Core 1.0 electric toothbrush review: this new budget model is still sustainable – and the one I’d buy
summary: With wireless charging, a battery that lasts up to four weeks and recyclable heads, Suri’s latest eco-friendly model doesn’t lose much in the cost-saving process
content: Last year’s Suri 2.0 toothbrush was a huge improvement on its predecessor. It fixed a handful of things that made the original hard for me to recommend, while continuing to focus on sustainability with recyclable heads made of cornstarch and castor oil. But that kind of innovation doesn’t come cheap, and the Suri 2.0 brush costs £105 with the charging case, or £85 without (an option that wasn’t available at launch). Now Suri has sought to tackle that problem with a cheaper brush: the Suri Core 1.0. It’s £65, and keeps the key improvements of Suri 2.0 (now rebranded as Suri Pro 2.0), making it a strong option for those who put sustainability at the top of their shopping priorities. View at Suri View at Boots *** How I tested Having tested more than 30 brushes for the Filter’s guide to the best electric toothbrushes, this isn’t my first toothbrushing rodeo, if you’ll excuse the confusing mental image. In short, you brush, brush and brush again – well beyond the twice-a-day recommendation of dentists and into obsessive territory. While brushing, I look for grip, how it feels in the mouth and – most importantly – how clean my teeth feel after use. That may sound pretty basic, but having tested so many electric toothbrushes, some really do feel more effective than others, and clearly cope better with stubborn plaque. Fortunately, Suri gave me the Core 1.0 brush two weeks ahead of launch day, so I’ve been using it every day since. I also have a Suri Pro 2.0 brush for direct comparison. *** Suri Core 1.0 electric toothbrush: what you need to know View at Suri View at Boots The Suri Core 1.0 is Suri’s first attempt at a lower-cost brush. Given the 1.0 in the title, it’s safe to assume it won’t be the last, either. Fortunately, the cost-cutting required to produce a cheaper toothbrush hasn’t seen a return to the weak spots of the now-retired first-generation Suri brush. The Suri Core 1.0 has a pressure sensor and a wireless charging cradle – not the more easily breakable spring-pin base of the original. It also uses the same cornstarch and castor oil heads that you can send back free for recycling. There’s also a two-minute timer with a friendly buzz every 30 seconds to remind you to move on to the next mouth quadrant. So what is it missing, exactly? The motor is slightly weaker, producing 28,000 sonic vibrations per minute, rather than the 30,000 on the Suri Pro 2.0, and the battery lasts up to four weeks, rather than more than four weeks as the more expensive model promises. Its plastic handle is made from more than 90% bio-circular material (including used cooking oil and other waste feedstocks), rather than the aluminium of previous models (it’s still IPX7 waterproof). But the biggest change is that the Suri Core 1.0 brush doesn’t come with a case. Granted, you can now buy the Suri Pro 2.0 without a case, but you can always buy one at a later date. Not so with the Suri Core 1.0: it’s slightly shorter than the more expensive model, so doesn’t fit snugly, and it won’t charge within it either. However, for travel, there’s a plant-based head cover included, and there’s a travel lock to stop it going off in your bag. All of this will set you back £65. For comparison, the Suri Pro 2.0 is £105 with a charging case, or £85 without. *** Suri Core 1.0 specifications Type: sonic Modes: two (clean and polish) Power: up to 28,000 BPM Pressure sensor? Yes Battery life: up to four weeks App? No Warranty: one year (extended to two years with registration) *** What we love The main thing to celebrate about the Suri Core 1.0 is how little the company has had to cut to make a cheaper brush. It would have been easy for the company to simply stuff the now-retired original Suri brush’s innards into the new bio-circular plastic shell, flaws and all. But Suri hasn’t done that: a pressure sensor and wireless charging – by far the biggest improvements in Suri Pro 2.0 over its predecessor – are present. Given I got through no fewer than three spring-pin chargers on my original brush, that’s quite a big deal. What’s more, if I were to do a blind test on the Suri Pro 2.0 and Suri Core 1.0 – something I’d not advise if you don’t want to spend the rest of the day cleaning your mirror – I’m not convinced I’d be able to tell the difference in performance either. The motor speed is only 6.7% lower, after all, and while the Suri Pro 2.0 is weightier and clearly more premium with its cold-to-the-touch aluminium finish, there’s not much in it. Trying both side by side reveals a similar feel, and a similar level of mouth cleanliness. And while the Core 1.0 has a battery life that’s “up to a month” rather than “over a month”, it doesn’t feel that this will make much of a difference in practical terms. Indeed, Suri tells me the Core 1.0 has a 700mAh cell to the Suri Pro 2.0’s 800mAh, so not a huge difference. And then, of course, there’s Suri’s main selling point: its sustainability credentials. Like its pricier sibling, the brush uses heads made from cornstarch with castor oil bristles. These can be sent back to Suri for recycling, with compostable postage-paid envelopes supplied to make the process as frictionless as possible. A pack of three costs £14.99, but you can subscribe and receive two every six months for £8.98 so you’re never stuck using a head past its best. The Core 1.0’s head is white, giving the brush a two-tone design with whichever base colour you pick. The heads are the same for every model, so there’s nothing stopping you getting a colour designed for the Suri Pro 2.0 instead – though it won’t exactly match the colour of the base. This is a deliberate design decision, according to Suri, to prevent people confusing the Core 1.0 with the 2.0. *** What we don’t love Tackling the elephant in the room first, is the lack of travel case a problem? chineseTitle: Suri Core 1.0 电动牙刷评测：这款新的预算模型仍然是可持续的——也是我会购买的一款
chineseSummary: 凭借无线充电、可持续使用长达四个星期的电池和可回收的充电头，Suri 最新的环保型号在节省成本的过程中并没有损失太多
chineseContent: 去年的 Suri 2.0 牙刷比其前身有了巨大的改进。它修复了一些让我很难推荐原版的问题，同时继续关注由玉米淀粉和蓖麻油制成的可回收头的可持续性。但这种创新并不便宜，Suri 2.0 刷子带充电盒的售价为 105 英镑，不带充电盒的售价为 85 英镑（该选项在发布时不提供）。现在，Suri 试图用更便宜的刷子来解决这个问题：Suri Core 1.0。它的售价为 65 英镑，保留了 Suri 2.0（现已更名为 Suri Pro 2.0）的关键改进，对于那些将可持续发展作为购物优先事项的人来说是一个不错的选择。查看 Suri View at Boots *** 我的测试方式 在 Filter 的最佳电动牙刷指南中测试了 30 多种牙刷后，这不是我第一次刷牙竞技表演，请原谅我的混乱心理形象。简而言之，你刷牙、刷牙、再刷牙——远远超出了牙医建议的每天两次的范围，进入了痴迷的领域。刷牙时，我会注意抓地力、口腔的感觉，以及最重要的是，使用后牙齿的清洁程度。这听起来可能很基本，但在测试了这么多电动牙刷后，有些电动牙刷确实比其他电动牙刷更有效，而且显然可以更好地应对顽固的牙菌斑。幸运的是，Suri 在发布前两周给了我 Core 1.0 刷子，所以从那以后我每天都在使用它。我还有一把Suri Pro 2.0刷子可以直接对比。 *** Suri Core 1.0 电动牙刷：您需要了解的信息 查看 Suri 查看 Boots Suri Core 1.0 是 Suri 首次尝试低成本牙刷。鉴于标题中的 1.0，可以肯定它也不会是最后一个。幸运的是，生产更便宜的嘟嘟声需要削减成本
